Laura —

Quick technical notes to address your questions (short bullet answers, plus an internal recommendation):

1) KV cache / session isolation:
- Dedicated pools: we can provide per-customer namespace isolation at the runtime layer (separate KV stores + enforced tenancy) but that requires an explicit contract addendum and we enable strict network policies. It does NOT guarantee the same physical isolation as private nodes.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full tenancy; KV sits inside your VPC or on-prem host and is under your control — simplest for PHI compliance.

2) On-prem (air-gapped) option:
- In scope: yes, we have an on-prem package used for a small set of regulated customers. Delta: +4–8 weeks procurement/provisioning vs VPC private, and +25–40% E2E TCO uplift driven by additional ops runbook & HSM integration. We'll need SOC evidence exchange + physical access windows for initial setup.

3) Canary & rollback mechanics:
- Canary lane runs model/version pinned artifacts using prefix-caching and a shadow-router. If regression triggers (quality / latency thresholds) we'll automatically flip traffic to the dedicated A100 fallback (compatible quantized variant). The router supports a gradual rollback or immediate cutover.
- We log every decision and can trigger an emergency rollback hook from the console or an API call.

Internal recommendation (for ArborCare's profile):
- Pilot: 8 H100 private (PHI routes) + 8 A100 dedicated (app traffic); focus pilot metrics on 99th ms latency, token/unit cost, and hallucination rate measured against your eval set.
- Production: hybrid slate where PHI routes run on private H100 and everything else runs on reserved A100. Keep 6–8 H100 in a canary pool for model rollouts.

Sizing delta (from workbook):
- The private H100 nodes are sized to handle ~3.4k tokens/sec aggregate (per 8-node pilot) and scale linearly with additional H100s.
- The dedicated A100 reserved slab (48 GPUs) sustains your projected 90 qps bursts with 20% headroom when sharded into 64-slice VM tiling.
